newsitem.title: USA: PSA tells panel bankruptcy law changes are needed.
newsitem.headline: PSA tells panel bankruptcy law changes are needed.

text.p: Leading bond market trade group, PSA, on Thursday called for changes in the U.S. Bankruptcy Code to reduce risks to the financial markets and to the firms that enter into financial transactions with customers that file for bankruptcy.

"Greater certainty and less risk would benefit debtors perhaps most of all, since it would mean readier and more efficient access to financial products and to capital, especially in times of stress," the association's General Counsel, Paul Saltzman told a special bankruptcy panel that met in Detroit.

The bond group's concerns follow its fight early last year to intervene in Orange County, California's bid to get a bankruptcy court to declare the county's reverse repurchase agreements with Merrill Lynch & Co null and void.

The Orange County case generated widespread concern among securities industry players who feared such a ruling would place the entire repurchase agreement market, with average daily volume of about $1.8 trillion, at risk.
Even other transactions including swaps and other privately negotiated derivatives could pose similar risks in times of bankruptcy, PSA has said.

At a special hearing before the National Bankruptcy Review Commission, an independent panel created by President Clinton after Congress enacted bankruptcy reforms in 1994, Saltzman delivered that message and asked the panel to recommend a series of changes to Congress.
"Innovation in the development of financial products in the trading markets in recent years have proviked considerable discussion of the concept of systemic risk," Saltzman said.
The bond group has already taken its own steps to help ensure certainty for the firms that enter into repurchase agreements.
Last September, PSA revised its widely used master repurchase agreement form to reflect market paractices and strengthen legal protections for firms.

The revamped form outlines the basic relationships, rights, and obligations of counterparties in the repo market. It also spells out that margin calls must be satisfied on the same day they are issued rather than the next day.
